sections.approach: I'll implement slugify() as a pipeline of transformations applied in the exact order specified. First, transliteration using a map for the specific characters (ß, ẞ, æ, Æ, ø, Ø, œ, Œ, đ, Đ, ł, Ł, þ, Þ, ð, Ð). This must happen before NFKD normalization to ensure proper handling. Second, apply NFKD normalization to decompose compatibility characters, then remove combining marks (U+0300-U+036F) using a regex. Third, remove apostrophes (both straight and curly) without inserting separators. Fourth, convert to lowercase. Fifth, split into words: identify runs of [a-z0-9] as words, with any character outside that set treated as a word boundary. Sixth, join words with the separator (default '-'), ensuring no leading, trailing, or repeated separators. Seventh, handle maxLength: if the slug exceeds maxLength, find the longest prefix of whole words that fits; if the first word alone exceeds maxLength, truncate it to maxLength characters. Eighth, handle empty or whitespace-only input by returning an empty string. Ninth, ensure idempotency by verifying that the pipeline produces the same output when reapplied. Tenth, validate input type and options, throwing appropriate errors. The implementation will be pure, deterministic, and efficient using string methods and regexes.
sections.edge_cases: Key edge cases: 1) Empty string or whitespace/punctuation-only input returns empty string. 2) Repeated separators in input should collapse to single separators in output. 3) Leading/trailing separators should be removed. 4) Transliteration of sharp s (ß/ẞ) to 'ss' and other specified characters. 5) Compatibility characters like ligatures (ﬁ -> fi), roman numerals (Ⅻ -> XII), and circled digits (① -> 1) via NFKD. 6) Non-Latin scripts (e.g., CJK) are removed as they become non-[a-z0-9] characters. 7) Apostrophes removed without separator insertion. 8) When maxLength is less than the first word length, truncate the first word. 9) Idempotency: slugify(slugify(x)) must equal slugify(x). 10) Invalid input (non-string) throws TypeError. 11) Invalid separator or maxLength throws RangeError. 12) Mixed separators in input (e.g., 'a_b-c.d') normalize to the chosen separator. 13) Case where maxLength exactly matches a word boundary. 14) Input with only separators returns empty string. 15) Combining marks removal after NFKD ensures clean base characters.
